sections.title: Problem Statement
sections.html:
Design a class to efficiently find the Kth largest element in a stream of numbers.

The class should have the following two things:

  1. The constructor of the class should accept an integer array containing initial numbers from the stream and an integer ‘K’.
  2. The class should expose a function add(int num) which will store the given number and return the Kth largest number.

sections.title: Solution
sections.html:
This problem follows the Top ‘K’ Elements pattern and shares similarities with Kth Smallest number.

We can follow the same approach as discussed in the ‘Kth Smallest number’ problem. However, we will use a Min Heap (instead of a Max Heap) as we need to find the Kth largest number.

sections.title: Code
sections.html:
Here is what our algorithm will look like:

Output

4th largest number is: 5 4th largest number is: 6 4th largest number is: 6

code.python3:
from heapq import *


class KthLargestNumberInStream:
  minHeap = []

  def __init__(self, nums, k):
    self.k = k
    # add the numbers in the min heap
    for num in nums:
      self.add(num)

  def add(self, num):
    # add the new number in the min heap
    heappush(self.minHeap, num)

    # if heap has more than 'k' numbers, remove one number
    if len(self.minHeap) > self.k:
      heappop(self.minHeap)

    # return the 'Kth largest number
    return self.minHeap[0]


def main():

  kthLargestNumber = KthLargestNumberInStream([3, 1, 5, 12, 2, 11], 4)
  print("4th largest number is: " + str(kthLargestNumber.add(6)))
  print("4th largest number is: " + str(kthLargestNumber.add(13)))
  print("4th largest number is: " + str(kthLargestNumber.add(4)))


main()

sections.title: Time complexity
sections.html: The time complexity of the add() function will be O(logK)O(logK)O(logK) since we are inserting the new number in the heap.

sections.title: Space complexity
sections.html: The space complexity will be O(K)O(K)O(K) for storing numbers in the heap.
